newsitem.title: USA: N.J. says imposes hiring freeze on state jobs.
newsitem.headline: N.J. says imposes hiring freeze on state jobs.

text.p: New Jersey has imposed an immediate hiring freeze for all state government positions, Personnel Commissioner Linda Anselmini said Monday.

Anselmini said the freeze is intended to reduce the state payroll in anticipation of the new budget year, which begins July 1 and to reserve job vacancies for the 700 to 1,235 state workers whose jobs are targeted for elimination in next year's budget.

Hundreds of state workers will be given formal notice at least 60 days before layoffs are announced, but the labor rules mean pink slips need not be final. Senior workers are permitted to "bump," or claim a similar post held by a more junior staffer.

In addition to the layoffs already announced, another 600 to 1,000 workers could lose their jobs in the final stage of closing the Marlboro Psychiatric Hospital and North Princeton Development Center.
